skill.name: mp-teach
skill.description: Use when you want to be taught a skill or concept over multiple sessions — a stateful teaching workspace of lessons, references, and learning records grounded in your mission.
whenToUse: You want to learn a topic or skill across multiple sessions, not one-off
You want interactive lessons grounded in high-trust sources, not the model's memory
You want your progress and insights captured so future sessions build on them
You want beautiful, reviewable reference materials and lessons

keyConcepts.explanation: The current directory holds the learning state: MISSION.md (why you care about the topic, grounds everything), reference/*.html (compressed cheat-sheets), RESOURCES.md, learning-records/*.md (insights driving future sessions), lessons/*.html, assets/*, and NOTES.md.

Deep learning needs knowledge (from high-trust resources), skills (interactive lessons you devise from that knowledge), and wisdom (from other learners/practitioners). Never trust parametric knowledge — populate RESOURCES.md first.

keyConcepts.term: Lessons are the unit of teaching
keyConcepts.explanation: A lesson is one self-contained, beautiful (Tufte-like) HTML file, short enough to complete quickly within working-memory limits, giving a single tangible win tied to the mission and inside the learner's zone of proximal development.

Fluency (in-the-moment retrieval) gives an illusory sense of mastery; storage strength (long-term retention) is the real goal. Design for desirable difficulty: retrieval practice, spacing, and interleaving.
Like ADRs for learning — numbered records (0001-...) capturing non-obvious lessons and key insights, used to calculate the zone of proximal development for the next session.

gotchas: Never trust parametric knowledge — ground teaching in high-trust resources captured in RESOURCES.md first
Keep lessons short — learners' working memory is small; one tangible win per lesson
Optimise for storage strength, not fluency; fluency can feel like mastery it hasn't earned
Interleaving is for skills practice only, not pure-knowledge topics
